findings.evidence: template/scripts/_platform_common.py (diff lines 349-361): `sys.excepthook = _report_platform_config_error` runs at module import. `_default=sys.excepthook` is captured once at import, so a hook installed later by another tool is bypassed or wrapped inconsistently. The hook only helps scripts that import the module before failing. An explicit `main()` wrapper would be more predictable.
findings.summary: Importing `_platform_common` replaces the process-wide `sys.excepthook`. This is an implicit global side effect, and it also affects non-entry-point importers such as tests and embedding tools.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_integration.py (diff lines 1060-1084): the old code defaulted `main_branch` and `paths.worktrees` when the file was absent. The new code calls `read_project_config`, which requires all 13 top-level keys and 14 table entries. Only `main_branch` and `paths.worktrees` are used here. scripts/sandboxed_writer_probes.py:94 still writes a minimal `main_branch = "main"` source-contract, so any consumer of that fixture that reaches this reader would now fail.
findings.summary: `_project_topology` used to tolerate a missing or partial `.dev-platform.toml`. It now needs the full schema, so a checkout holding an older or minimal contract fails with a wrapped `RequirementIntegrationError`.
